title: Parallel Trends as a Spectrum
abstract: arXiv:2610.31978v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Difference-in-differences (DiD) designs are typically used to identify and estimate average causal effects, even though treatment can affect the entire outcome distribution. This has led to a growing interest in distributional DiD methods. However, identifying the full counterfactual distribution requires a parallel trends assumption on the entire distributional dynamics, which can be too strong in practice. We address this problem by introducing a spectrum of identifying restrictions that lie between the average and fully distributional DiD by imposing parallel trends on $L$-moments. This corresponds to a basis expansion of the distributional dynamics. Importantly, each $L$-moment is interpretable as familiar distributional components: location, dispersion, skewness, kurtosis, etc. Researchers can pick and choose which features they want to target. translated_title: 平行趋势作为一个谱系
translated_abstract: 双重差分（DiD）设计通常被用于识别和估计平均因果效应，尽管处理效应可能影响整个结果分布。这引发了人们对分布型DiD方法日益增长的兴趣。然而，识别完整的反事实分布需要对整个分布动态施加平行趋势假设，这在实践中可能过于严格。我们通过引入一系列介于平均DiD和完全分布DiD之间的识别约束来解决这一问题，即在 $L$ 矩上施加平行趋势假设。这对应于分布动态的基展开。重要的是，每个 $L$ 矩都可以解释为人们熟悉的分布成分：位置、离散度、偏度、峰度等。研究者可以自由选择想要关注的目标特征。例如，第二 $L$ 矩可以识别基尼平均差，但不能重新（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文提出了一个基于 $L$ 矩平行趋势假设的谱系识别框架，在平均DiD与完全分布DiD之间提供灵活过渡，使研究者能够按需选择关注分布的特定特征（如位置、离散度、偏度、峰度等）。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a spectrum of identifying restrictions based on parallel trends in $L$-moments, bridging average and fully distributional DiD methods and allowing researchers to flexibly target specific distributional features such as location, dispersion, skewness, and kurtosis.
